title: John Calvin
source: Public domain. Consolidated from John Calvin, Commentary on Philippians, Colossians, and Thessalonians, translated by John Pringle, Calvin Translation Society, and the Institutes of the Christian Religion, translated by Henry Beveridge; both as published by the Christian Classics Ethereal Library.
body: John Calvin on Second Thessalonians, chapter 2. In his Commentary on Philippians, Colossians, and Thessalonians, in the John Pringle translation, Calvin writes at Second Thessalonians 2, verse 1: Now I beseech you, by the coming. It may indeed be read, as I have noted on the margin, concerning the coming, but it suits better to view it as an earnest entreaty, taken from the subject in hand, just as in 1 Corinthians 15:31, when discoursing as to the hope of a resurrection, he makes use of an oath by that glory which is to be hoped for by believers. In the Institutes of the Christian Religion, in the Henry Beveridge translation, Calvin draws on this chapter again in Book 4, chapter 7.
